name: rhetorical_situations
description: Bitzer's triangle expanded into working categories: the exigences that call writing into being, models of the audience it addresses, the venues and genres it must inhabit, the classical occasions and their modern descendants, the constraints that bound what can be said, and the personae an author can adopt.

exigence_types.name: crisis event
exigence_types.definition: A sudden harmful occurrence that demands immediate public response and suspends normal deliberation.
exigence_types.effect: Grants instant attention and licenses direct address.
exigence_types.caution: The window closes fast, and early facts are usually wrong.

exigence_types.name: new evidence
exigence_types.definition: A study, dataset, or document that unsettles the standing account and obliges someone to reconcile it.
exigence_types.effect: Justifies revisiting a question the audience thought settled.

exigence_types.name: policy window
exigence_types.definition: Kingdon's moment when the problem, policy, and politics streams converge and a proposal can actually pass.
exigence_types.caution: Windows are short; arguments written for a closed window read as stale.

exigence_types.name: pending decision
exigence_types.definition: A vote, ruling, purchase, or hire about to be made, which the writing means to inform or change.
exigence_types.effect: Supplies a natural deadline and a defined decider.

exigence_types.name: scandal disclosure
exigence_types.definition: Revelation of wrongdoing that creates a demand for explanation, apology, or accountability.
exigence_types.caution: Invites moralizing that outruns the established facts.

exigence_types.name: public misconception
exigence_types.definition: A widely held belief the writer takes to be false, whose persistence is itself the urgency.
exigence_types.effect: Frames the piece as correction rather than novelty.
exigence_types.caution: Repeating the myth to refute it can entrench it.

exigence_types.name: scholarly gap
exigence_types.definition: An unexamined question or unstudied population in a literature, offered as warrant for new work.
exigence_types.caution: A gap alone is not a reason; the gap must matter.

exigence_types.name: contradiction in the literature
exigence_types.definition: Two credible bodies of work reaching incompatible conclusions, which someone must reconcile.
exigence_types.effect: Sets up a natural adjudicating structure.

exigence_types.name: misapplied precedent
exigence_types.definition: A rule, ruling, or prior case being extended to facts it was never meant to cover.

exigence_types.name: litigation filed
exigence_types.definition: A complaint, motion, or appeal that obliges responsive argument on a court's schedule.

exigence_types.name: regulatory comment period
exigence_types.definition: A formal open interval in which an agency must receive and answer written objections.
exigence_types.effect: Guarantees a reader of record, which rewards specificity over rhetoric.

exigence_types.name: release of a work
exigence_types.definition: The publication or shipment of a book, film, product, or standard, which occasions review and appraisal.

exigence_types.name: death of a public figure
exigence_types.definition: A death that calls for obituary, eulogy, or reassessment of a life's work.
exigence_types.caution: Decorum constrains candor; the honest assessment often has to wait.

exigence_types.name: anniversary
exigence_types.definition: A dated recurrence — of a founding, an atrocity, a discovery — that licenses retrospective writing.
exigence_types.effect: Manufactures timeliness for a subject that has none.
exigence_types.caution: Readers recognize the peg; the piece must earn more than the date.

exigence_types.name: technological arrival
exigence_types.definition: A new capability whose appearance forces reconsideration of practices built around its absence.
exigence_types.caution: Encourages inflated novelty claims about continuities.

exigence_types.name: shift made visible by data
exigence_types.definition: A demographic, economic, or environmental change that a new release of numbers makes undeniable.
exigence_types.effect: Lets the argument begin from a fact the audience cannot dispute.

exigence_types.name: rival publication
exigence_types.definition: A piece so wrong, or so influential, that leaving it unanswered would concede the field.
exigence_types.effect: Supplies a ready-made opponent and structure.
exigence_types.caution: Amplifies the target; sometimes silence is the stronger move.

exigence_types.name: request for proposals
exigence_types.definition: A funder's or client's solicitation that defines the question, the format, and the deadline.

exigence_types.name: call for papers
exigence_types.definition: A conference or journal invitation that sets a theme and a submission window.

exigence_types.name: onboarding need
exigence_types.definition: New people repeatedly needing the same orientation, which documentation exists to absorb.
exigence_types.effect: Defines the reader precisely: someone at hour one.

exigence_types.name: recurrent failure
exigence_types.definition: A problem that has happened more than once, making a written postmortem the price of not repeating it.

exigence_types.name: moral outrage
exigence_types.definition: A shared sense of violated norms seeking articulation and a target.
exigence_types.caution: The most available energy and the least durable; outrage-driven pieces age badly.

exigence_types.name: rumor requiring correction
exigence_types.definition: An unverified claim spreading fast enough that its correction becomes urgent.
exigence_types.caution: Correction can broadcast the rumor to people who had not heard it.

exigence_types.name: leadership transition
exigence_types.definition: A change of officeholder that reopens settled questions and invites agenda-setting.
exigence_types.effect: Legitimizes proposals that would otherwise seem like second-guessing.

exigence_types.name: calendared ritual
exigence_types.definition: An annual report, budget cycle, or state-of-the-field address whose occasion is simply that it is time.
exigence_types.caution: Ritual exigence produces ritual prose unless a real question is imported.

exigence_types.name: personal experience newly generalizable
exigence_types.definition: A private episode the writer comes to see as an instance of something public.
exigence_types.caution: The generalization must be argued, not asserted by adjacency.

exigence_types.name: the unremarked-upon
exigence_types.definition: A silence, absence, or normalized condition that the writer treats as the scandal.
exigence_types.effect: Strong for essays and criticism; the piece must supply its own urgency.

exigence_types.name: a question asked
exigence_types.definition: A direct request from a reader, student, client, or interviewer that the writing answers.
exigence_types.effect: Guarantees a real audience with a real want.

exigence_types.name: unmet obligation of the record
exigence_types.definition: A promise, prediction, or commitment made publicly that has come due for accounting.

exigence_types.name: manufactured exigence
exigence_types.definition: Urgency produced by publicity or coordinated campaign rather than by events.
exigence_types.caution: Writing to it lends real attention to an artificial problem; name it as such instead.

audience_models.name: hostile expert
audience_models.definition: A reader who knows the field as well as the writer and wants the argument to fail.
audience_models.effect: Forces precise concession, tight citation, and anticipatory rebuttal.
audience_models.caution: Writing only to this reader produces defensive, unreadable prose.

audience_models.name: sympathetic novice
audience_models.definition: A reader who wants the writer to be right but lacks the background to follow shorthand.
audience_models.effect: Rewards analogy, worked examples, and glossing on first use.

audience_models.name: mixed jury
audience_models.definition: A heterogeneous decision-making body spanning expertise, priors, and interest.
audience_models.effect: Pushes toward layered argument: a narrative anyone can follow with technical support beneath it.
audience_models.caution: Averaging the audience produces prose that lands with none of it.

audience_models.name: universal audience
audience_models.definition: Perelman and Olbrechts-Tyteca's construct: all reasonable people, as the writer imagines them, used as a test of argument quality.
audience_models.effect: Filters out appeals that work only on partisans.

audience_models.name: particular audience
audience_models.definition: A specific group with known commitments, addressed on the premises it actually holds.
audience_models.caution: Arguments tuned to a particular audience embarrass the writer when they travel.

audience_models.name: self as audience
audience_models.definition: Deliberation addressed to oneself, which Perelman treats as a limiting case of argumentation.

audience_models.name: gatekeeper
audience_models.definition: An editor, peer reviewer, or program officer who must approve before any other reader sees the work.
audience_models.effect: Imposes genre compliance as a precondition of being read at all.

audience_models.name: the undecided middle
audience_models.definition: Readers with no fixed position who will be moved by whichever side seems more reasonable.
audience_models.effect: Rewards visible fairness and steelmanning over point-scoring.

audience_models.name: the committed base
audience_models.definition: Readers who already agree and read for confirmation, ammunition, and solidarity.
audience_models.effect: Good for mobilization, useless for persuasion.
audience_models.caution: Base-directed writing is the main engine of unearned certainty.

audience_models.name: the opposition's persuadables
audience_models.definition: Members of the other side whose commitments are weaker than their tribe's.
audience_models.effect: Requires arguing from their premises rather than one's own.

audience_models.name: overhearing audience
audience_models.definition: People not addressed but present, who judge the exchange rather than participate in it.
audience_models.effect: The real target of most public debate; how one treats the opponent is the argument.

audience_models.name: downstream audience
audience_models.definition: Readers who encounter the work quoted, excerpted, or summarized rather than whole.
audience_models.caution: Any sentence that survives alone should be one the writer would defend alone.

audience_models.name: adversarial cross-examiner
audience_models.definition: A reader hunting for the one overstatement that discredits everything else.
audience_models.effect: Disciplines quantifiers, hedges, and scope claims.

audience_models.name: the skimmer
audience_models.definition: A reader who takes headings, first sentences, and figures and nothing else.
audience_models.effect: Argues for load-bearing topic sentences and self-sufficient captions.

audience_models.name: the deep reader
audience_models.definition: A reader who will follow a long chain of reasoning and notice inconsistency across chapters.
audience_models.effect: Permits deferred payoff and structural callbacks.

audience_models.name: the busy decision-maker
audience_models.definition: An executive or official who reads only until the decision is clear.
audience_models.effect: Demands the answer first, Minto-style, with support after.

audience_models.name: lay jury of peers
audience_models.definition: Ordinary citizens deciding a technical matter under formal rules of evidence.
audience_models.effect: Rewards narrative coherence and credible witnesses over statistical nuance.

audience_models.name: discourse community
audience_models.definition: Swales's specialist group sharing goals, genres, and a lexis, whose conventions signal membership.
audience_models.caution: Its shorthand is exclusionary to everyone outside it.

audience_models.name: interdisciplinary audience
audience_models.definition: Specialists from several fields, each expert in something and novice in the rest.
audience_models.caution: Every field's jargon is another field's obstacle; no single register satisfies all.

audience_models.name: the future reader
audience_models.definition: Whoever finds the work in an archive after the occasion has passed.
audience_models.effect: Argues for dating claims and spelling out context that is currently obvious.

audience_models.name: the implied reader
audience_models.definition: Iser's reader inscribed in the text itself — the competence and disposition the writing presupposes.

audience_models.name: the authorial audience
audience_models.definition: Rabinowitz's hypothetical audience the author wrote for, whose knowledge the text takes for granted.

audience_models.name: the narrative audience
audience_models.definition: Rabinowitz's role the reader plays inside the fiction, treating its events as fact.

audience_models.name: the ideal reader
audience_models.definition: The single imagined person, sometimes a real acquaintance, whom the writer writes to.
audience_models.effect: A practical device for fixing register and level of assumed knowledge.

audience_models.name: the resistant reader
audience_models.definition: Fetterley's reader who refuses the text's assumed sympathies and reads against its grain.

audience_models.name: captive audience
audience_models.definition: Readers required to be there — students, employees, jurors — who cannot leave but can disengage.
audience_models.caution: Attention is compelled, not earned, which conceals bad writing.

audience_models.name: self-selected audience
audience_models.definition: Readers who sought the work out and share its premises by the act of arriving.
audience_models.effect: Permits starting further in; less setup required.

audience_models.name: the client
audience_models.definition: A reader who commissioned the work and will judge it against a brief and an interest.

audience_models.name: the funder
audience_models.definition: A reader deciding whether to pay for the work described, judging feasibility as much as merit.

audience_models.name: the regulator
audience_models.definition: An official reader assessing compliance, whose questions are fixed in advance by rule.
audience_models.effect: Rewards a structure that maps onto the rule.

audience_models.name: the aggrieved stakeholder
audience_models.definition: A reader with a personal stake in the subject who will scrutinize how they are characterized.
audience_models.caution: Getting their situation slightly wrong forfeits every other point.

audience_models.name: the translated reader
audience_models.definition: A reader who will meet the work in another language and cultural frame.
audience_models.caution: Wordplay, idiom, and local reference are the first casualties.

audience_models.name: the acquiring editor
audience_models.definition: A publisher's editor deciding whether to buy the book, who reads the proposal for a category and a market before reading the pages for merit.
audience_models.effect: Forces the writer to state what shelf the work sits on and who is already buying that shelf.
audience_models.caution: Writing to this reader alone produces a proposal that sells and a book nobody finishes.

audience_models.name: the trade reviewer
audience_models.definition: A professional reviewer writing to a word limit for booksellers and librarians, reading fast and against the conventions of the announced category.
audience_models.effect: Rewards a clear category promise kept, and punishes hybrids that cannot be described in one sentence.
audience_models.caution: Two hundred words of judgement reach more people than the book does; the first fifty pages carry it.

audience_models.name: the bookstore browser
audience_models.definition: A reader deciding in under two minutes, from cover, flap copy, and one opened page, whether to buy.
audience_models.effect: Puts weight on the first page of every chapter, not only the first page of the book.
audience_models.caution: Optimizing every opening for the browser produces a book of hooks with no middle.

audience_models.name: the classroom adopter
audience_models.definition: An instructor judging the work as an assignable text: level, length, apparatus, and whether it teaches across a term.
audience_models.effect: Values chapter self-sufficiency, discussable questions, and an index that supports assigning parts.
audience_models.caution: Adoption is decided by structure and price as much as by argument.

audience_models.name: the audiobook listener
audience_models.definition: A reader who receives the work only as sound, with no page to turn back to, no figures, and no visible headings.
audience_models.effect: Makes cadence, signposting, and named antecedents load-bearing, since nothing can be re-scanned.
audience_models.caution: Tables, parenthetical asides, and long numeric strings do not survive narration; see the narration channel.

audience_models.name: the citation checker
audience_models.definition: A reader who follows the notes to the sources to see whether they say what the text claims they say.
audience_models.effect: Sets the true standard for a citation: not that it exists, but that it supports the sentence attached to it.
audience_models.caution: A single misrepresented source discredits every unchecked one.

audience_models.name: the quoting reader
audience_models.definition: A reader who will lift one sentence out and carry it elsewhere, where it must stand without its paragraph.
audience_models.effect: Rewards claims written to survive extraction — self-contained, qualified in place, not dependent on the previous sentence.
audience_models.caution: The sentence most likely to be quoted is the most overstated one; write it to be quotable and defensible.

audience_models.name: the second-time reader
audience_models.definition: A reader who already knows how it ends and is reading for how it was set up.
audience_models.effect: Pays off plants, motifs, and early qualifications that the first reading passed over.
audience_models.caution: Nothing may depend on this reader; a payoff only they can see is a payoff nobody gets.

audience_models.name: the search algorithm
audience_models.definition: The non-human first reader: retrieval, recommendation, and model-training systems that index the work and decide which humans are shown it.
audience_models.effect: Makes titles, subtitles, headings, and keywords part of the rhetorical situation rather than packaging.
audience_models.caution: Writing for the index degrades the prose; the metadata dossier is the place to serve it.

venue_and_genre.name: op-ed
venue_and_genre.definition: A short signed argument in a general-interest outlet, one claim defended against the obvious objection.
venue_and_genre.caution: Length forces a single point; two points make neither.

venue_and_genre.name: letter to the editor
venue_and_genre.definition: A very short published response correcting or extending a previously published piece.

venue_and_genre.name: news report
venue_and_genre.definition: An account of what happened, sourced and attributed, with the writer's judgment kept out of the sentences.

venue_and_genre.name: feature article
venue_and_genre.definition: A longer reported piece organized around character and scene rather than the day's news.

venue_and_genre.name: investigative long-read
venue_and_genre.definition: An extended reported argument that documents wrongdoing or systemic failure from primary evidence.
venue_and_genre.caution: Every load-bearing sentence must survive a lawyer's read.

venue_and_genre.name: magazine essay
venue_and_genre.definition: A discursive nonfiction piece that thinks in public, blending reportage, argument, and voice.

venue_and_genre.name: personal essay
venue_and_genre.definition: An essay whose evidence is the writer's own experience, arranged toward a general insight.
venue_and_genre.caution: Without the turn to something larger it stays anecdote.

venue_and_genre.name: criticism
venue_and_genre.definition: Evaluative writing that judges a work against a stated standard and shows the reasoning.

venue_and_genre.name: book review
venue_and_genre.definition: A short account of what a book attempts, whether it succeeds, and whether the attempt was worth making.

venue_and_genre.name: blog post
venue_and_genre.definition: Self-published writing with no gatekeeper, free in length and register, dated and revisable.
venue_and_genre.caution: The absence of an editor is felt by readers before it is felt by writers.

venue_and_genre.name: newsletter issue
venue_and_genre.definition: Recurring writing delivered to subscribers, whose form is shaped by cadence and accumulated relationship.

venue_and_genre.name: social thread
venue_and_genre.definition: A serialized argument in short posts, each of which must stand alone and pull to the next.
venue_and_genre.caution: Fragments circulate without the thread; the weakest unit defines the reception.

venue_and_genre.name: forum comment
venue_and_genre.definition: A contribution to a running asynchronous discussion, addressed to prior posts and read by lurkers.

venue_and_genre.name: technical documentation
venue_and_genre.definition: Writing that lets a reader accomplish a task with a system, judged only by whether they succeed.
venue_and_genre.effect: Voice is a liability; completeness and ordering are the craft.

venue_and_genre.name: tutorial
venue_and_genre.definition: A guided sequence that takes a beginner from nothing to a working result by doing.

venue_and_genre.name: reference entry
venue_and_genre.definition: A lookup-oriented description of one thing, complete in itself and not meant to be read in order.

venue_and_genre.name: design document
venue_and_genre.definition: A proposal describing a problem, alternatives considered, and a chosen approach, written to be argued with.

venue_and_genre.name: postmortem
venue_and_genre.definition: A blameless account of a failure, its causes, and the changes that follow.
venue_and_genre.caution: Passive voice becomes evasion when the point is accountability.

venue_and_genre.name: whitepaper
venue_and_genre.definition: A quasi-technical document that explains a problem and positions a solution, usually with commercial intent.
venue_and_genre.caution: Readers discount it as marketing unless the evidence is checkable.

venue_and_genre.name: monograph
venue_and_genre.definition: A book-length scholarly treatment of a single subject by one author.

venue_and_genre.name: edited-volume chapter
venue_and_genre.definition: A contribution written to a collection's theme and to an editor's frame.

venue_and_genre.name: journal article
venue_and_genre.definition: A peer-reviewed report of original research, usually in IMRaD arrangement.

venue_and_genre.name: literature review
venue_and_genre.definition: A synthesis of existing work that maps positions and locates an opening.

venue_and_genre.name: systematic review
venue_and_genre.definition: A review with a pre-registered protocol, explicit inclusion criteria, and reproducible search.
venue_and_genre.effect: Method transparency substitutes for the reviewer's authority.

venue_and_genre.name: conference paper
venue_and_genre.definition: A short research report written for a deadline and a talk, often reporting work in progress.

venue_and_genre.name: dissertation
venue_and_genre.definition: A book-length demonstration of research competence written for a committee before any other reader.
venue_and_genre.caution: Its examination genre and its book genre are not the same document.

venue_and_genre.name: grant proposal
venue_and_genre.definition: An argument that a question matters, that a plan will answer it, and that this team can execute it.
venue_and_genre.effect: Reviewers score against published criteria; structure should mirror them.

venue_and_genre.name: business memo
venue_and_genre.definition: Internal writing that states a recommendation, its basis, and what it asks of the reader.

venue_and_genre.name: executive summary
venue_and_genre.definition: A standalone condensation that must convey the decision without the document behind it.
venue_and_genre.caution: It is not an introduction; it is the whole argument at one-tenth scale.

venue_and_genre.name: board deck
venue_and_genre.definition: Slides prepared for a governing body, where the appendix carries the evidence and the page carries the ask.

venue_and_genre.name: pitch deck
venue_and_genre.definition: A short persuasive slide sequence aimed at investment, structured around problem, solution, and traction.

venue_and_genre.name: press release
venue_and_genre.definition: An announcement written for journalists in inverted-pyramid form, designed to be quoted.

venue_and_genre.name: policy brief
venue_and_genre.definition: A short document translating research into options for a decision-maker with no time and no background.
venue_and_genre.effect: Recommendation-first; the analysis exists to survive challenge, not to lead.

venue_and_genre.name: legislative testimony
venue_and_genre.definition: Prepared written and spoken remarks to a legislative body, followed by questioning.

venue_and_genre.name: regulatory comment
venue_and_genre.definition: A formal submission to an agency during rulemaking, which the agency must consider on the record.
venue_and_genre.effect: Specific, cited objections create legal obligations; rhetoric does not.

venue_and_genre.name: amicus brief
venue_and_genre.definition: A filing by a non-party offering the court context or consequences the parties will not supply.
venue_and_genre.caution: Repeating a party's brief wastes the one thing amicus status offers.

venue_and_genre.name: appellate brief
venue_and_genre.definition: A written argument to a reviewing court, confined to the record and to preserved issues.

venue_and_genre.name: judicial opinion
venue_and_genre.definition: A court's written explanation of its holding, which binds or persuades future cases.

venue_and_genre.name: contract
venue_and_genre.definition: Operative language that creates obligations, read adversarially and interpreted against the drafter.
venue_and_genre.caution: Elegance is irrelevant; ambiguity is the only real defect.

venue_and_genre.name: keynote address
venue_and_genre.definition: A framing talk that sets an event's theme, aimed at orientation and morale more than instruction.

venue_and_genre.name: conference talk
venue_and_genre.definition: A timed spoken presentation of work to peers, with questions after.

venue_and_genre.name: lightning talk
venue_and_genre.definition: A very short talk admitting exactly one idea and one example.

venue_and_genre.name: sermon
venue_and_genre.definition: An address expounding a text and applying it to a congregation's life.

venue_and_genre.name: eulogy
venue_and_genre.definition: A speech honoring the dead, addressed to the living, that gives a life a shape.

venue_and_genre.name: commencement address
venue_and_genre.definition: A ceremonial speech to graduates, conventionally offering counsel by way of narrative.
venue_and_genre.caution: The most convention-bound occasion in public speech.

venue_and_genre.name: toast
venue_and_genre.definition: A very short ceremonial speech at a gathering, praising a person or an occasion.

venue_and_genre.name: podcast interview
venue_and_genre.definition: Extended recorded conversation where argument emerges through exchange rather than composition.

venue_and_genre.name: documentary narration
venue_and_genre.definition: Voiceover written to accompany images, carrying only what the picture cannot.

venue_and_genre.name: screenplay
venue_and_genre.definition: A script in industry format specifying only what an audience will see and hear.

venue_and_genre.name: stage play
venue_and_genre.definition: A dramatic script for live performance, where scale, exposition, and time obey the theater's limits.

venue_and_genre.name: short story
venue_and_genre.definition: A prose fiction of a single sitting, usually one turn and few characters.

venue_and_genre.name: novel
venue_and_genre.definition: Book-length prose fiction, long enough to sustain multiple arcs and a developed world.

venue_and_genre.name: manifesto
venue_and_genre.definition: A declarative statement of principles and intent, written to recruit rather than to persuade skeptics.
venue_and_genre.caution: Its refusal to hedge is the genre, and also its limit.

venue_and_genre.name: open letter
venue_and_genre.definition: A letter addressed to one party and published for another, whose real audience is the onlooker.

venue_and_genre.name: petition
venue_and_genre.definition: A request for action whose force comes from the count of signatories rather than the argument.

venue_and_genre.name: syllabus
venue_and_genre.definition: A course document that is simultaneously a plan, a contract, and an argument about what matters.

venue_and_genre.name: textbook chapter
venue_and_genre.definition: Instructional exposition of settled knowledge, sequenced for learners and shorn of controversy.
venue_and_genre.caution: Consensus framing hides the live disputes that make a field interesting.

venue_and_genre.name: lecture
venue_and_genre.definition: Sustained spoken exposition to students, paced for note-taking and structured by recap.

venue_and_genre.name: encyclopedia entry
venue_and_genre.definition: A neutral summary of established knowledge on one topic, attributed and non-original.

venue_and_genre.name: obituary
venue_and_genre.definition: A published account of a life just ended, part news report and part appraisal.

venue_and_genre.name: annual report
venue_and_genre.definition: A periodic institutional account of performance, part disclosure and part self-presentation.
venue_and_genre.caution: The compulsory parts are read; the narrative parts usually are not.

venue_and_genre.name: cover letter
venue_and_genre.definition: A short self-presentation that argues fit between a person and a specific position.

venue_and_genre.name: personal statement
venue_and_genre.definition: An applicant's narrative of formation and purpose, judged on coherence as much as content.

venue_and_genre.name: recommendation letter
venue_and_genre.definition: A third-party assessment whose conventions make understatement read as criticism.

occasion_types.name: deliberative
occasion_types.definition: Aristotle's genus concerned with future action, arguing what a body should or should not do.
occasion_types.effect: Its topics are the expedient and the harmful.

occasion_types.name: forensic
occasion_types.definition: Aristotle's genus concerned with past acts, arguing accusation and defense.
occasion_types.effect: Its topics are the just and the unjust.

occasion_types.name: epideictic
occasion_types.definition: Aristotle's genus of display, concerned with the present, distributing praise and blame and reinforcing shared values.
occasion_types.effect: Consolidates a community's commitments rather than deciding anything.

occasion_types.name: encomium
occasion_types.definition: Formal praise of a person, thing, or quality, one of the progymnasmata exercises.

occasion_types.name: invective
occasion_types.definition: Formal blame, the paired opposite of encomium.
occasion_types.caution: Reads as unserious unless the charges are specific and sourced.

occasion_types.name: funeral oration
occasion_types.definition: Praise of the dead that turns into instruction for the living, as in Pericles and Lincoln.

occasion_types.name: commemoration
occasion_types.definition: Speech or writing marking an anniversary, which re-narrates a past event for present purposes.
occasion_types.caution: Whose memory is being consolidated is always a live question.

occasion_types.name: inaugural
occasion_types.definition: An address at the assumption of office, defining a tenure's terms before any action.

occasion_types.name: apologia
occasion_types.definition: A formal self-defense of character or conduct in response to accusation.
occasion_types.caution: Denial, differentiation, transcendence, and apology are distinct strategies with different costs.

occasion_types.name: jeremiad
occasion_types.definition: A lament that a community has fallen from its founding standards, coupled with a call to return.
occasion_types.effect: Powerful and structurally conservative; its ideal always lies in the past.

occasion_types.name: protreptic
occasion_types.definition: Exhortation urging an audience toward a way of life or a discipline.

occasion_types.name: deliberation in committee
occasion_types.definition: Structured group decision-making under rules of order, where procedure shapes what can be argued.

occasion_types.name: policy debate
occasion_types.definition: Formal contest over a proposition of policy with assigned sides and stock issues.
occasion_types.effect: Its stock issues — harm, inherency, solvency, disadvantages — organize much nonfiction argument.

occasion_types.name: adjudicative hearing
occasion_types.definition: A proceeding in which a neutral decides a contested matter on a record, under rules of evidence.

occasion_types.name: commission of inquiry
occasion_types.definition: A chartered investigation that establishes an authoritative account of a past failure.
occasion_types.effect: The modern descendant of forensic rhetoric at institutional scale.

occasion_types.name: product launch
occasion_types.definition: An announcement occasion mixing epideictic display with deliberative appeal to adopt.

occasion_types.name: performance review
occasion_types.definition: A recurring evaluative occasion combining praise, blame, and forward-looking direction.
occasion_types.caution: Its blended genres are why so much of it says nothing.

occasion_types.name: retrospective
occasion_types.definition: A backward-looking assessment at a set interval, judging what was done against what was intended.

occasion_types.name: award citation
occasion_types.definition: A very short epideictic text naming precisely what is being honored and why.

occasion_types.name: dedication
occasion_types.definition: A short text consecrating a work, place, or building to a person or purpose.

occasion_types.name: call to action
occasion_types.definition: A mobilizing occasion that converts shared conviction into a specific next step.
occasion_types.caution: Fails when the step is unspecified or beyond the audience's power.

occasion_types.name: confession
occasion_types.definition: A first-person disclosure of fault whose credibility depends on offering more than was demanded.

occasion_types.name: testimony
occasion_types.definition: First-person witness offered as evidence, whose authority is presence rather than analysis.
occasion_types.caution: Its moral force resists cross-examination, which is exactly why it is used.

occasion_types.name: negotiation
occasion_types.definition: An exchange occasion where argument is instrumental to agreement rather than to truth.
occasion_types.effect: Concession is a move, not a defeat.

occasion_types.name: didactic occasion
occasion_types.definition: Teaching, where the aim is the audience's later competence rather than present assent.

occasion_types.name: state-of-the-field address
occasion_types.definition: A survey occasion in which a discipline narrates its own progress and sets an agenda.
occasion_types.caution: Epideictic wearing deliberative clothes; the praise is doing the arguing.

constraint_types.name: word or time limit
constraint_types.definition: A hard ceiling on length or duration that forces selection before it forces style.
constraint_types.effect: The first real editorial decision is what to leave out.

constraint_types.name: format template
constraint_types.definition: A required structure — section headings, forms, slide masters — the writing must fill.
constraint_types.caution: Templates get filled rather than used; the argument can vanish into the boxes.

constraint_types.name: house style guide
constraint_types.definition: An outlet's binding rules on usage, citation, and mechanics.

constraint_types.name: genre convention
constraint_types.definition: The reader's learned expectations for a form, which can be met, bent, or broken at a price.
constraint_types.effect: Meeting them buys attention to spend on the parts that are new.

constraint_types.name: review and approval
constraint_types.definition: A chain of people who must sign off, each of whom can subtract but rarely add.
constraint_types.caution: Predicting the objection and pre-softening the prose is how institutional writing dies.

constraint_types.name: legal exposure
constraint_types.definition: Defamation, privacy, and contempt risk that limits what can be asserted about whom.

constraint_types.name: embargo
constraint_types.definition: An agreed date before which information cannot be published.
constraint_types.effect: Permits preparation but forbids the timing advantage.

constraint_types.name: confidentiality obligation
constraint_types.definition: A contractual or professional duty that bars the use of specific knowledge the writer holds.
constraint_types.caution: Writing around a hole is visible; better to name the constraint.

constraint_types.name: classification level
constraint_types.definition: A formal secrecy tier controlling what may be written and who may read it.

constraint_types.name: anonymity requirement
constraint_types.definition: Blind review or source protection that removes the writer's or subject's identity from the text.
constraint_types.effect: Strips ethos, forcing the argument to carry itself.

constraint_types.name: disclosure requirement
constraint_types.definition: A duty to state funding, conflicts, or affiliations that colors how claims are received.

constraint_types.name: citation norms
constraint_types.definition: A field's rules for what must be attributed and how much prior work must be acknowledged.
constraint_types.caution: Under-citation reads as ignorance; over-citation reads as insecurity.

constraint_types.name: accessibility requirement
constraint_types.definition: Obligations such as alt text, reading order, and contrast that constrain how content may be presented.
constraint_types.effect: Forces every visual argument to have a linguistic equivalent.

constraint_types.name: localization burden
constraint_types.definition: The cost imposed on translated or internationalized text, which penalizes idiom and cultural reference.

constraint_types.name: reading-level target
constraint_types.definition: A mandated comprehension grade that limits sentence length and lexical choice.
constraint_types.caution: Optimizing the metric can destroy the precision it was meant to protect.

constraint_types.name: assumed prior knowledge
constraint_types.definition: What the audience already has, which determines how much must be built before the argument starts.
constraint_types.effect: Misjudging it upward loses readers; downward insults them.

constraint_types.name: medium affordances
constraint_types.definition: What the channel permits — print permanence, screen scroll, audio linearity, no footnotes aloud.
constraint_types.effect: Audio and print reward opposite handling of qualification and enumeration.

constraint_types.name: distribution algorithm
constraint_types.definition: A platform's ranking system, which rewards particular openings, lengths, and affects.
constraint_types.caution: Writing to it optimizes for reach at the cost of the argument's shape.

constraint_types.name: paywall
constraint_types.definition: Access restriction that determines who can read past the opening and who only sees the headline.

constraint_types.name: character limit
constraint_types.definition: A platform ceiling that forces compression, abbreviation, and serialization.
constraint_types.caution: Compression reads as confidence; hedges are the first thing cut and the first thing missed.

constraint_types.name: institutional voice
constraint_types.definition: Writing on behalf of an employer or body, where first person and personal judgment are unavailable.

constraint_types.name: funder expectations
constraint_types.definition: The priorities of whoever pays, which shape what questions can be asked and how results are framed.

constraint_types.name: political feasibility
constraint_types.definition: The bound on which recommendations can be made seriously in a given moment.
constraint_types.caution: Treating it as fixed makes analysis a servant of the status quo.

constraint_types.name: decorum
constraint_types.definition: The classical fit among speaker, subject, audience, and occasion — what is fitting rather than merely permitted.
constraint_types.effect: Violating it deliberately is a rhetorical move with a known cost.

constraint_types.name: taboo
constraint_types.definition: A subject or term that cannot be raised directly without the audience refusing the rest.
constraint_types.caution: Circumlocution around it is usually more conspicuous than naming it.

constraint_types.name: deadline
constraint_types.definition: The time available, which caps research, revision, and verification.
constraint_types.effect: Often the binding constraint that all other constraints are blamed on.

constraint_types.name: the available evidence
constraint_types.definition: What can actually be documented, which limits what may be claimed regardless of what is believed.

constraint_types.name: prior commitments on the record
constraint_types.definition: Positions the writer has already published, which constrain revision without an explicit accounting.
constraint_types.effect: Openly changing one's mind is stronger than quietly not mentioning it.

constraint_types.name: hostile monitoring
constraint_types.definition: The certainty that opponents will excerpt the least defensible sentence.
constraint_types.caution: Defensive writing against this produces prose with no sentences worth quoting at all.

constraint_types.name: production budget
constraint_types.definition: Money and rights available for figures, images, permissions, and design, which limit the visual argument.

constraint_types.name: the rhetor's standing
constraint_types.definition: The credentials, position, and history the audience knows, which license some claims and bar others.
constraint_types.effect: Determines whether a claim needs argument or merely assertion.

author_personae.name: the expert
author_personae.definition: A persona grounded in credential and command of the literature, claiming the right to be believed.
author_personae.effect: Compresses argument; a citation can replace a demonstration.
author_personae.caution: Any error is disproportionately costly to this persona.

author_personae.name: the eyewitness
author_personae.definition: A persona whose authority is having been there, reporting what was seen rather than what is known.

author_personae.name: the guide
author_personae.definition: A persona who knows the territory and walks the reader through it at the reader's pace.
author_personae.effect: Makes difficulty feel navigable rather than diminishing.

author_personae.name: the skeptic
author_personae.definition: A persona who withholds assent and tests claims, including the writer's own.
author_personae.caution: Doubt without a positive account eventually reads as evasion.

author_personae.name: the convert
author_personae.definition: A persona who once held the opposing view and narrates the change, using former error as evidence.
author_personae.effect: Disarms the reader who currently holds that view.

author_personae.name: the insider
author_personae.definition: A persona speaking from within an institution, trading access for the constraints of membership.
author_personae.caution: Readers discount the parts that would cost the insider something.

author_personae.name: the outsider
author_personae.definition: A persona with no stake in the field's settlements, licensed to ask the naive question.
author_personae.caution: Unearned outsider status reads as ignorance dressed as independence.

author_personae.name: the everyman
author_personae.definition: A persona claiming ordinary standing and common sense against specialists.
author_personae.caution: Frequently a costume worn by the very expert it disclaims.

author_personae.name: the ironist
author_personae.definition: A persona whose stated position is not the held position, inviting the reader into the gap.
author_personae.caution: Excerpted or translated, irony inverts into its literal meaning.

author_personae.name: the prophet
author_personae.definition: A persona who denounces a present decline and warns of consequence, speaking for a violated standard.
author_personae.caution: Wears out; unfulfilled warnings discount the next one.

author_personae.name: the reasonable moderate
author_personae.definition: A persona positioned between camps, whose authority is visible fairness to both.
author_personae.caution: The midpoint is set by whoever staked the extremes.

author_personae.name: the advocate
author_personae.definition: A persona openly arguing for one side and asking to be judged by the argument, not by neutrality.
author_personae.effect: Honest partisanship costs less credibility than concealed partisanship.

author_personae.name: the honest broker
author_personae.definition: Pielke's persona that expands the range of options a decision-maker can see without choosing among them.

author_personae.name: the reporter
author_personae.definition: A self-effacing persona that keeps out of the sentences and lets sources and scenes carry the account.

author_personae.name: the essayist
author_personae.definition: Montaigne's persona of a mind trying something out in public, whose changes of direction are the content.
author_personae.caution: Requires a mind worth watching; performance of thinking is not thinking.

author_personae.name: the curmudgeon
author_personae.definition: A persona of practiced impatience with fashion, cant, and enthusiasm.
author_personae.caution: One register only; cannot express admiration credibly.

author_personae.name: the enthusiast
author_personae.definition: A persona of open delight in the subject, recruiting by transmitted interest.
author_personae.caution: Undifferentiated praise makes every judgment worthless.

author_personae.name: the teacher
author_personae.definition: A persona organized around the reader's understanding, willing to repeat, sequence, and check.
author_personae.caution: Slides into condescension when the reader is not actually a student.

author_personae.name: the fellow sufferer
author_personae.definition: A persona who shares the reader's predicament rather than solving it from outside.

author_personae.name: the penitent
author_personae.definition: A persona accounting for a personal failure, whose credibility rests on conceding more than required.
author_personae.caution: Confession used instrumentally is recognized and resented.

author_personae.name: the investigator
author_personae.definition: A persona structured by the pursuit of an answer, taking the reader along the search rather than to its result.

author_personae.name: the synthesist
author_personae.definition: A persona whose contribution is assembly — reading across fields and showing what they add up to.
author_personae.caution: Must be scrupulous about attribution or it reads as appropriation.

author_personae.name: the contrarian
author_personae.definition: A persona defined against consensus, whose value depends on being right often enough to matter.
author_personae.caution: Predictable inversion is as lazy as predictable agreement.

author_personae.name: the institutionalist
author_personae.definition: A persona defending procedure, precedent, and slow correction against urgency.

author_personae.name: the practitioner
author_personae.definition: A persona whose authority is having done the work, speaking from craft rather than study.
author_personae.effect: Concrete detail is its native evidence.

author_personae.name: the eiron
author_personae.definition: The classical self-deprecator who feigns less knowledge than they hold and lets the reader outpace them.
author_personae.effect: The reader who arrives at the conclusion first believes it more.

author_personae.name: the alazon
author_personae.definition: The classical boaster who claims more than they are, used as a foil rather than adopted sincerely.
author_personae.caution: Adopted unironically it is the least persuasive posture in rhetoric.

author_personae.name: the translator
author_personae.definition: A persona standing between a specialist community and a general readership, accountable to both.
author_personae.caution: Simplification the field would disown destroys the standing that makes the persona work.

author_personae.name: the moral witness
author_personae.definition: A persona whose claim is to have seen suffering and to be obliged to report it.

author_personae.name: the amicus
author_personae.definition: A persona of the interested non-party, offering context and consequence rather than advocacy for either side.

author_personae.name: the archivist
author_personae.definition: A persona whose authority is custody of the record, arguing by producing the document.
author_personae.effect: Restraint amplifies; the evidence is meant to speak.

author_personae.name: the ranter
author_personae.definition: A persona of undisguised anger that abandons decorum for force.
author_personae.caution: Sustains a page, rarely a chapter, and forfeits the undecided reader.
